survey: A classic flying saucer seen from above at a three-quarter angle, tilted slightly toward the viewer. Main parts: (1) a brushed-steel saucer body, a shallow cone that rises toward the centre; (2) a dark gunmetal ring around the edge that frames the body; (3) a green glass hemisphere for the cockpit, sitting in a raised steel collar at the centre of the cone, with the collar going all the way round the dome's base; (4) about ten orange glowing lights set into the rim ring at roughly even spacing. The spacing widens toward the front, as perspective requires, and the lights at the back are hidden behind the dome where you would expect. The saucer floats against a plain yellow background, which fits a flying craft, so it needs no support. The saucer and rim are an even ellipse, the dome is centred on the body for this viewing angle, and nothing passes through or melts into anything else. Rim lights and a glass dome are standard parts of a stylised UFO, not invented additions.
